s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness with urinary retention and cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
key_facts: MRI brain and orbits showed no abnormality
MRI spine showed nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated red blood cell count

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness with urinary retention and cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
key_facts: MRI brain and orbits showed no abnormality
MRI spine showed nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated red blood cell count

shortlist.label: Acute myeloid leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis) and elevated atypical cells/blasts in cerebrospinal fluid analysis

shortlist.label: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white blood cell count and presence of atypical cells/blasts in cerebrospinal fluid analysis

shortlist.label: Myeloid sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots on MRI spine, consistent with myeloid sarcoma

shortlist.label: Granulocytic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to myeloid sarcoma, granulocytic sarcoma is a tumor composed of immature granulocytic cells, which could explain the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Neurolymphomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of cranial nerves and presence of atypical cells/blasts in cerebrospinal fluid analysis, suggesting lymphomatous infiltration of the nervous system

raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis), severe flaccid quadriparesis, reduced muscle stretch reflexes, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing 98% atypical cells/blasts are highly suggestive of leukemia, and the specific findings of nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots on MRI spine are consistent with leukemic infiltration, which is more commonly seen in acute myeloid leukemia.

rejected.label: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
rejected.why: Less likely due to the presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions, which are more commonly associated with myeloid lineage leukemias

rejected.label: Myeloid sarcoma
rejected.why: Although myeloid sarcoma can present with similar symptoms, the presence of 98% atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid and the systemic nature of the symptoms suggest a more disseminated disease process, such as acute myeloid leukemia

rejected.label: Granulocytic sarcoma
rejected.why: Granulocytic sarcoma is another term for myeloid sarcoma, and the same reasoning applies

rejected.label: Neurolymphomatosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and nerve roots, but the presence of 98% atypical cells/blasts with myeloid features and the systemic symptoms suggest a myeloid lineage leukemia rather than lymphoma
